features.name: Self-hosted install
features.summary: One Helm chart installs the whole platform on your own Kubernetes cluster.

features.name: Platform backups from the console
features.summary: Back up the platform database from the admin console, optionally with the encryption keys under a passphrase, then download it.

features.name: New-release notices
features.summary: The admin console tells you when a newer Vista Platform release exists and links to its release notes.

features.name: One-click update
features.summary: Update the platform from the admin console with a backup first, a verified chart and a one-click rollback.

features.name: Network sensors
features.summary: A lightweight sensor on your network captures traffic and reports what it sees.

features.name: Roles and permissions
features.summary: Role-based access control for every user, with invitations for new members.

features.name: Audit log
features.summary: Every administrative and security-relevant action is recorded and searchable.

features.name: API tokens and MCP server
features.summary: API tokens, and a read-only MCP server that lets AI agents query your inventory.

features.name: Single sign-on
features.summary: Sign in through your own identity provider (OIDC or SAML) with group-to-role mapping.

features.name: Passive network discovery
features.summary: Finds hosts, services and the cryptography they use from observed traffic.

features.name: Active scan
features.summary: Probe the assets you choose for their TLS, SSH and certificate details on demand.

features.name: Network device interrogation
features.summary: Reads crypto configuration directly from firewalls, load balancers and switches.

features.name: Cloud discovery
features.summary: Inventories certificates, keys and endpoints in AWS, Azure and Google Cloud.

features.name: PCAP upload
features.summary: Upload a packet capture and get the same inventory a live sensor would produce.

features.name: Spreadsheet import
features.summary: Bring an existing asset list in from a spreadsheet.

features.name: Unified asset inventory
features.summary: One record per real asset, with lenses for infrastructure, certificates, keys and more.

features.name: One identity for every sighting
features.summary: Every discovery path identifies a device the same way, explains key and address changes, and lets you link or pin what it cannot tell.

features.name: Network and crypto map
features.summary: See every device by site and network, marked by the crypto it serves.

features.name: Software inventory
features.summary: Installed software from host agents and SBOM uploads, tied to the assets running it.

features.name: Certificates, keys and crypto configurations
features.summary: Every certificate, key and TLS/SSH configuration, linked to where it is used.

features.name: Certificate trust
features.summary: Decide which CAs you trust; every certificate is classed public, trusted, self-signed, untrusted or distrusted, so what you never agreed to trust is findable.

features.name: Third-party connections
features.summary: Tracks the external services your hosts talk to, and the crypto those connections use.

features.name: Asset lifecycle and freshness
features.summary: Shows when each asset was last seen, and retires what is no longer there.

features.name: OT / ICS discovery
features.summary: Active probing and an inventory view for Modbus, DNP3, BACnet and other OT protocols.

features.name: Business Units
features.summary: Nested owners (department, customer, cost centre) on assets and prefixes, with import and query support.

features.name: Interfaces
features.summary: Every asset's network interfaces with MAC and IP addresses, filled by discovery or entered by hand.

features.name: Networks (IPAM)
features.summary: Prefixes, IP addresses, ranges and VRFs as a tree with utilisation, free space and address lookup.

features.name: VLANs
features.summary: VLAN groups and VLANs, with the prefixes and interfaces that carry them.

features.name: Cabling and cable tracing
features.summary: Every cable with both ends, a faceplate per device, bulk cable editing, and port traces through patch panels, tinted by the crypto behind each port.

features.name: Power panels, feeds and power cabling
features.summary: Power panels and feeds at each site, power ports and PDU outlets with their draws, and power traces from a server through its PDU to the feed.

features.name: Spares, stock and RMA
features.summary: Spare parts in stock at site locations with quantities, installs from the shelf into assets, parts removed to stock, and return cases to replacement.

features.name: Rack power budget and PDU collection
features.summary: Each rack's power budget per feed and leg, a power overlay on the elevation, and measured outlet draw and state from APC, Raritan and Eaton PDUs.

features.name: Physical cabling on the map
features.summary: The map draws cables between devices beside their observed relationships, and any relationship seen on a port can show the physical path behind it.

features.name: Change log on assets
features.summary: Who changed what, from where and when, plus a journal of dated notes on each object.

features.name: Cloud account approval
features.summary: A cloud account is an asset you approve once; its resources are then admitted automatically or queued for review.

features.name: Rack elevations
features.summary: Front and rear elevations of every rack — drag devices into place, see reserved units, and tint each device by its worst open crypto finding.

features.name: Floor plans
features.summary: A grid floor plan per location with racks dragged into place and coloured by unit or power utilisation.

features.name: Facilities dashboard
features.summary: Free rack space per site, fullest racks, switches and prefixes nearing full, and the ageing cabling backlog, each linking to its list.

features.name: Sites and locations
features.summary: Regions, site groups, sites and the locations inside them, with a page per site and assets placed on it.

features.name: Device types and catalogue
features.summary: A seeded catalogue of 154 device types, manufacturers, roles and platforms, instantiating interface and port templates when applied.

features.name: Asset commercial lifecycle
features.summary: Purchase, cost, warranty, support contract and install dates per asset, with warranty and end-of-support states from device type and platform dates.

features.name: Modules and virtual chassis
features.summary: Module types and bays, inventory items and stacked-switch virtual chassis on each asset's Hardware tab.

features.name: Virtual device contexts
features.summary: VDOMs, vsys, VDCs and route domains, discovered from FortiGate, Palo Alto, F5 and Nexus or declared, with the interfaces each owns.

features.name: Circuits
features.summary: Providers, provider networks and circuits with terminations that cable to your ports.

features.name: Virtual circuits
features.summary: SD-WAN, MPLS L3VPN and Metro Ethernet overlays on a provider network, with the interfaces that terminate them as peer, hub or spoke.

features.name: VLAN translation and ASN ranges
features.summary: VLAN translation policies and rules that interfaces apply, and the ASN ranges a registry delegated, with the numbers still free in each.

features.name: Virtualisation
features.summary: Clusters and their hosts, virtual machines and disks, grouped by cluster type.

features.name: VPN tunnels and policy
features.summary: Tunnel groups, tunnels and terminations, with the IKE and IPsec policy each uses.

features.name: Wireless LANs and links
features.summary: WLAN groups, WLANs with their authentication type, and point-to-point wireless links.

features.name: Contacts
features.summary: Contacts and roles assigned to any object, plus image attachments.

features.name: Custom fields
features.summary: Tenant-defined fields on assets, interfaces, prefixes and VLANs, validated on every write and usable in queries.

features.name: Config contexts
features.summary: Weighted JSON contexts assigned by site, role or platform and merged per asset.

features.name: Saved filters and export templates
features.summary: Saved filters for every object kind and text templates that render any list for export.

features.name: Bulk import and export
features.summary: CSV import with dry run and CSV export for every DCIM object kind, under Settings → Infrastructure.

features.name: Crypto risk assessment
features.summary: Scores every crypto configuration against a standards-anchored algorithm catalogue.

features.name: Post-quantum readiness
features.summary: Shows which cryptography is quantum-vulnerable and tracks migration progress.

features.name: Compliance frameworks and findings
features.summary: Continuous evaluation against built-in frameworks, with findings for every failure.

features.name: DCIM hygiene controls
features.summary: Inventory Hygiene controls for racking, rack positions, stale planned and unconfirmed cables, untyped interfaces, duplicate addresses, warranty and support.

features.name: Regulated frameworks
features.summary: SOC 2, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, NIST CSF and IEC 62351-3, delivered as a signed content bundle.

features.name: Custom compliance policies
features.summary: Write your own frameworks, controls and measurement rules for internal standards.

features.name: Threshold overrides
features.summary: Tune the measurement thresholds of the frameworks you have activated.

features.name: CBOM generation
features.summary: Immutable, content-hashed cryptographic bills of materials for any scope of assets.

features.name: CycloneDX export
features.summary: Download any CBOM as a standard CycloneDX 1.7 document.

features.name: Signed CBOMs, attestation and comparison
features.summary: Signed artifacts with compliance attestation, SPDX and PDF export, and drift comparison.

features.name: Remediation and ticketing
features.summary: Alerts, a work queue and plans, with tickets linked to the assets and findings they fix.

features.name: Inventory change notifications and webhooks
features.summary: Send inventory changes, filtered by object kind and action, to a webhook, Slack or email through routing rules.

features.name: CMDB / ITSM sync
features.summary: Two-way sync with ServiceNow, Device42, SolarWinds and Oomnitza, with dry run and undo.

features.name: CMDB sync — DCIM classes
features.summary: Push racks, networks, IP addresses, circuits, VLANs, network adapters and datacenters to ServiceNow and Device42 as their own CI classes, each switchable.

features.name: NetBox connector
features.summary: Pull sites, prefixes, VLANs and devices from NetBox and see where reality differs.

features.name: NetBox two-way sync
features.summary: Sync Business Units, IPAM and Interfaces with NetBox in both directions, field by field, with conflicts left to a person.

features.name: NetBox sync — circuits, virtualisation, VPN, wireless
features.summary: Sync circuits, clusters, VPN tunnels and policies, and wireless LANs with NetBox both ways, one switch per class; keys never cross.

features.name: NetBox sync — sites, racks, device catalogue, modules
features.summary: Sync sites, racks, device types and their templates, device placement, modules and virtual chassis with NetBox, field by field.

features.name: NetBox sync — ports and cables
features.summary: Sync console, patch-panel and power ports and cables with NetBox both ways; far ends not yet here wait, and LLDP proposals sync once approved.

features.name: NetBox sync — virtual circuits, ASN ranges, VLAN translation
features.summary: Sync NetBox 4.2's virtual circuits, ASN ranges and VLAN translation policies both ways, with each interface's policy, under their own switch.

features.name: NetBox sync — virtual machines
features.summary: Sync NetBox virtual machines, VM interfaces and virtual disks both ways as assets; new VMs pass your approval policy, pending ones never push.

features.name: Device42 import
features.summary: Import Device42's sites, racks, devices in their rack units, cabling, IP space and circuits, planned in a dry run first.

features.name: SIEM export
features.summary: Forward audit events to Splunk, Elastic, Datadog or a webhook.

features.name: Tenant isolation
features.summary: Row-level security in the database keeps every tenant's data separate.

features.name: Encrypted service mesh
features.summary: Mutual TLS between every platform service and its datastores.

features.name: Posture, never key material
features.summary: We record which algorithms a device uses, never the keys it uses them with.

features.name: Signed releases
features.summary: Every image, chart and binary is signed, with an SBOM and build provenance you can verify.

features.name: Readable source
features.summary: Core is built in public from source anyone can read and rebuild.

features.name: Continuous security scanning
features.summary: Static analysis on every change and nightly vulnerability scans of the published images.

features.name: Code-signed Windows binaries
features.summary: Authenticode-signed sensor and agent binaries for Windows.
